first: चौ॰ – मोर कहा सुनि करहु उपाई। होइहि ईस्वर करिहि सहाई॥
en: Brahma said, 'Listen to my advice and act on it; God will help and the work will be done. Sati, who gave up her body at Daksha's sacrifice, has been born again in the house of Himachal.'

first: तेहि तप कीन्ह सम्भु पति लागी। सिव समाधि बैठे सब त्यागी॥
en: 'She has done penance to win Shiva as her husband, but Shiva has left everything and sits in deep meditation. Though this is a great difficulty, still hear one idea of mine.'

first: पठवहु काम जाइ सिव पाहीँ। करइ छोभ सङ्कर मन माहीं॥
en: 'Send Kama, the god of love, to Shiva to stir up his mind. Then we will go, bow our heads to Shiva and make him agree to the marriage.'

first: एहि विधि भलेहि देव हित होई। मत अति नीक कहइ सब कोई॥
en: 'In this way the good of the gods may well come about.' Everyone said this was an excellent plan. The gods praised Kama with great feeling, and the god with five arrows and the fish banner appeared.

first: दो॰ – सुरन्ह कही निज बिपति सब, सुनि मन कीन्ह बिचार।
en: The gods told Kama all their troubles. Hearing them, he thought it over, smiled, and said, 'To oppose Shiva will not end well for me.'

first: चौ॰ – तदपि करब मैं काज तुम्हारा। स्रुति कह परम-धरम-उपकारा॥
en: 'Still, I will do your work, for the Vedas say that helping others is the highest duty. The good always praise one who gives up his body for the sake of others.'

first: अस कहि चलेउ सबहि सिर नाई। सुमन धनुष कर सहित सहाई॥
en: Saying this, he bowed to them all and set off with his helpers, the flower bow in his hand. As he went, Kama thought in his heart, 'Fighting Shiva means certain death for me.'

first: तब आपन प्रभाव विस्तारा। निज बस कीन्ह सकल संसारा॥
en: Then he spread out his power and brought the whole world under his control. The moment the fish-bannered god grew angry, all the limits set by the Vedas were swept away in an instant.

first: ब्रह्मचर्ज ब्रत सञ्जम नाना। धीरज धरम ज्ञान बिज्ञाना॥
en: Celibacy, vows, self-control of many kinds, patience, duty, knowledge, wisdom, good conduct, prayer, yoga and detachment: the whole army of Discernment ran away in fear.

first: भागेउ बिबेक सहाय सहित सो सुभट सञ्जुग-महि मुरे।
en: Discernment and his helpers fled; those brave warriors turned back from the battlefield and hid in the caves of the mountains of holy books. The world was thrown into confusion: 'O Creator, what will happen, and who will save us? Who has two heads, that the lord of Rati has angrily taken bow and arrow against him?'

first: दो॰ – जे सजीव जग चर अचर, नारि पुरुष अस नाम।
en: All living beings in the world, moving or still, that are called male or female, gave up their proper limits and fell under the power of desire.

first: चौ॰ – सब के हृदय मदन अभिलाखा। लता निहारि नवहिं तरु साखा॥
en: Desire filled every heart. Branches of trees bent down on seeing the creepers. Rivers swelled and rushed to the ocean, and ponds and pools ran together.

first: जहँ असि दसा जड़न्ह कै बरनी। को कहि सकइ सचेतन्ह करनी॥
en: When even lifeless things are described in such a state, who can tell what living beings did? Beasts and birds of the sky, water and land, all fell to desire and forgot the right season.

first: मदन-अन्ध ब्याकुल सब लोका। निसि दिन नहिँ अवलोकहि कोका॥
en: The whole world was blind with desire and restless. The chakwa birds no longer noticed whether it was night or day. Gods, demons, men, kinnaras, serpents, ghosts, goblins, spirits and vetalas...

first: इन्ह की दसा न कहेउँ बखानी। सदा काम के चेरे जानी॥
en: I have not described their state in detail, knowing them to be always the slaves of desire. Even siddhas, ascetics, great sages and yogis fell under desire and suffered the pain of separation.

first: भये काम-बस जोगीस तापस, पाँवरनि की को कहै।
en: When even the lords of yoga and the ascetics fell under desire, what can be said of common people? Those who saw God in all things now saw only women everywhere. Women saw the world full of men, and men saw it full of women. For a short while, Kama played this game throughout the universe.

first: सो॰ – धरा न काहूँ धीर, सब के मन मनसिज हरे।
en: No one kept his steadiness; Kama stole every mind. Only those whom Rama protected were saved at that time.

first: चौ॰ – उभयघरी अस कौतुक भयऊ। जब लगि काम सम्भु पहिँ गयऊ॥
en: This show lasted for about an hour, until Kama reached Shiva. On seeing Shiva, Kama grew afraid, and the whole world went back to its normal state.

first: भये तुरत सब जीव सुखारे। जिमि मद उतरि गये मतवारे॥
en: At once all beings became calm and happy, like drunk men when the drink wears off. Kama felt fear on seeing Rudra, the Lord who is hard to attack and hard to reach.

first: फिरत लाज कछु करिनहिं जाई। मरन ठानि मन रचेसि उपाई॥
en: He was ashamed to turn back and could do nothing, so he made up his mind to die and made a plan. At once he brought forth lovely Spring, king of the seasons, his friend, who shone in trees full of fresh flowers.

first: बन उपबन बापिका तड़ागा। परम सुभग सब दिसा विभागा॥
en: Forests, gardens, wells and lakes, and every side of the land, became most beautiful. Love seemed to be overflowing everywhere, so that even a dead man's heart would wake to desire.

first: जागेउ मनोभव मुयेहु मन बन, ‒ सुभगता न परइ कही।
en: Desire woke even in dead hearts; the beauty of the forest cannot be told. A cool, fragrant, gentle breeze blew, the true friend of the fire of love. Many lotuses bloomed in the lakes, with swarms of lovely bees humming over them. Swans, cuckoos and parrots sang sweetly, and nymphs sang and danced.

first: दो॰ – सकल कला करि कोटि बिधि, हारेउ सेन समेत।
en: Kama tried every art in millions of ways and was beaten with all his army. When Shiva's firm meditation did not break, the god born in the heart grew angry.

first: चौ॰ – देखि रसाल बिटप बर साखा। तेहि पर चढ़ेउ मदन मन माखा॥
en: Seeing a fine branch of a mango tree, Kama climbed onto it in anger. He fixed his arrows on his flower bow, took aim in great rage and drew the string back to his ear.

first: छाँडेउ विषम बान उर लागे। छूटि समाधि सम्भु तब जागे॥
en: He let fly his sharp arrows; they struck Shiva's heart. His meditation broke and Shiva woke. A great disturbance arose in the Lord's mind, and he opened his eyes and looked in every direction.

first: सौरभ-पल्लव मदन बिलोका। भयउ कोप कम्पेउ त्रैलोका॥
en: He saw Kama among the mango leaves. Shiva grew angry, and the three worlds shook. Then Shiva opened his third eye, and at his glance Kama was burnt to ashes.

first: हाहाकार भयउ जग भारी। डरपे सुर भये असुर सुखारी॥
en: A great cry of grief rose in the world. The gods were afraid and the demons were glad. Pleasure-seekers grieved, thinking of the joys of love, while seekers and yogis were freed from a thorn in their path.

first: जोगी अकंटक भये पति-गति, सुनत रति मुरछित भई।
en: The yogis were freed from trouble, but when Rati heard of her husband's fate she fainted. Weeping and crying out in many ways, she went to Shiva. With great love she pleaded in many ways and stood before him with joined hands. The gracious Lord Shiva, quick to be pleased, looked at the helpless woman and spoke these words.

first: दो॰ – अब तेँ रति तव नाथ कर, होइहि नाम अनङ्ग।
en: 'Rati, from now on your husband will be called Ananga, the bodiless one. Without a body he will still reach everyone. Now hear how you will meet him again.'

first: चौ॰ – जन जदुबंस कृष्न अवतारा। होइहि हरन महा महि भारा॥
en: 'When Krishna is born in the Yadu family to remove the great burden of the earth, your husband will be born as Krishna's son. My word will not prove false.'

first: रति गवनी सुनि सङ्कर बानी। कथा अपर अब कहउँ बखानी॥
en: Hearing Shiva's words, Rati went away. Now I will tell the rest of the story. When the gods heard all this news, Brahma and the others went to Vaikuntha.

first: सब सुर बिष्नु बिरञ्जि समेता। गये जहाँ सिव कृपा-निकेता॥
en: Then all the gods, with Vishnu and Brahma, went to where Shiva, the home of mercy, was. Each of them praised him in turn, and Shiva, who wears the moon, was pleased.

first: बोले कृपासिन्धु बृषकेतू। कहहु अमर आयहु केहि हेतू॥
en: Shiva, ocean of mercy, whose banner bears the bull, said, 'Tell me, gods, why have you come?' Brahma said, 'Lord, you know all hearts; still, out of devotion, I make my request.'

first: दो॰ – सकल सुरन्ह के हृदय अस, सङ्कर परम उछाह।
en: 'O Shankar, all the gods have one great longing in their hearts: Lord, they wish to see your wedding with their own eyes.'

first: चौ॰ – यह उत्सव देखिय भरि लोचन। सोह कछु करहु मदन-मद-मोचन॥
en: 'O destroyer of Kama's pride, please do something so that we may watch this festival to our hearts' content. Ocean of mercy, you did very well to burn Kama and then give a boon to Rati.'

first: सासति करि पुनि करहिँ पसाऊ। नाथ प्रभुन्ह कर सहज-सुभाऊ॥
en: 'Lord, it is the natural way of the great to punish first and then show kindness. Parvati has done boundless penance; now please accept her.'

first: सुनि विधि बिनय समुझि प्रभु बानी। ऐसइ होउ कहा सुख मानी॥
en: Hearing Brahma's request and understanding the Lord's wish, Shiva happily said, 'So be it.' Then the gods beat their drums, rained flowers and cried, 'Victory, victory to the lord of the gods!'

first: अवसर जानि सप्तरिषि आये। तुरतहि बिधि गिरि-भवन पठाये॥
en: Knowing the time was right, the seven sages came, and Brahma sent them at once to Himachal's home. First they went to where Bhavani was, and spoke sweet words filled with trickery.

first: दो॰ – कहा हमार न सुनेहु तब, नारद के उपदेस।
en: 'You did not listen to us then, because of Narada's advice. Now your vow has come to nothing, for Shiva has burnt Kama.'

first: चौ°—सुनि बोली मुसुकाइ भवानी। उचित कहेउ मुनिबर बिज्ञानी॥
en: Hearing this, Bhavani smiled and said, 'Wise great sages, you have spoken well. You think Shiva has burnt Kama only now, and that until now he was open to desire.'

first: हमरे जान सदा सिव जोगी। अज अनवद्य अकाम अभोगी ॥
en: 'But as I know him, Shiva is always a yogi, unborn, faultless, free of desire and untouched by pleasure. If I have served Shiva knowing him to be so, with love in deed, mind and speech,'

first: तौ हमार पन सुनहु मुनीसा। करिहहिँ सत्य कृपानिधि ईसा ॥
en: 'then hear, great sages, the gracious Lord will make my vow come true. As for what you said, that Hara has burnt Kama, that is a great mistake on your part.'

first: तात अनल कर सहज सुभाऊ। हिम तेहि निकट जाइ नहिँ काऊ ॥
en: 'Dear sir, it is the nature of fire that frost can never come near it; if it goes near, it surely melts away. The same is true of Kama and Shiva.'

first: दो॰—हिय हरषे मुनि बचन सुनि, देखि प्रीति बिस्वास ।
en: The sages were glad at heart to hear her words and to see her love and faith. They bowed to Bhavani and went to Himachal.

first: चौ॰—सबप्रसङ्गगिरि पतिहि सुनावा। मदन दहन सुनि अति दुख पावा ॥
en: They told the mountain king the whole story. He was very sad to hear that Kama had been burnt, but when they told him of the boon to Rati, Himavan felt great joy.

first: हृदय बिचारि सम्भू प्रभुताई। सादर मुनिवर लिये बोलाई॥
en: Thinking in his heart of Shiva's greatness, he respectfully called the learned sages. He had them find a good day, a lucky star and a fitting hour, and quickly fixed the wedding time by Vedic rule.

first: पत्री सप्तरिषिन्ह सो दीन्ही। गहि पद विनय हिमाचल कीन्ही॥
en: Himachal gave the wedding letter to the seven sages and, holding their feet, made his request. They went and gave the letter to Brahma, and as he read it his heart could not hold its joy.

first: लगन बाँचि बिधि सबहि सुनाई। हरषे सुनि सत्र सुर समुदाई॥
en: Brahma read out the wedding date to everyone, and the whole company of gods rejoiced to hear it. Flowers rained from the sky, music played, and holy pots were set up in all ten directions.

first: दो॰—लगे सँवारन सकल सुर, बाहन बिविध विमान॥
en: All the gods began to decorate their mounts and many kinds of sky-chariots. Happy, good omens appeared, and the nymphs sang.

first: चौ॰—सिवहि सम्भुगन करहिँ सिँगारा। जटा-मुकुट अहि-मौर सँवारा॥
en: Shiva's attendants began to dress him. They arranged his matted hair as a crown with a wedding crest of snakes. He wore snakes as earrings and bracelets, ash on his body, and a lion's skin around his waist.

first: ससि ललाट सुन्दर सिर गङ्गा। नयन-तीनि उपबीत-भुजङ्गा॥
en: The moon on his forehead, the lovely Ganga on his head, three eyes, a snake as his sacred thread, poison in his throat, and a garland of human skulls on his chest: though his dress looks unholy, the kind Shiva is the home of all good.

first: कर त्रिसूल अरु डमरु विराजा। चले बसह चढ़ि बाजहिँ बाजा॥
en: A trident and a damaru drum shone in his hands. He rode out on his bull while music played. Seeing Shiva, the goddesses smiled and said, 'There is no bride in the world fit for such a groom!'

first: बिष्नु बिरच्जि आदि सुर ब्राता। चढ़ि चढ़ि बाहन चले बराता॥
en: Vishnu, Brahma and the crowds of gods rode on their mounts in the wedding party. The company of gods was matchless in every way, but the party did not suit the groom.

first: दो॰—बिष्नु कहा अस बिहँसि तब, बोलि सकल दिसिराज।
en: Then Vishnu smiled, called all the guardians of the directions, and said, 'Let each of you walk separately, with your own group.'

first: चौ॰—बर अनुहारि बरात न भाई। हँसी करइहउ पर पुर जाई॥
en: 'Brothers, this party does not match the groom. Do you want to be laughed at in a strange city?' Hearing Vishnu's words the gods smiled and moved apart, each with his own troop.

first: मनहीँ मन महेस मुसुकाहीँ। हरि के व्यङ्ग बचन नहिँ जाहीं॥
en: Shiva smiled in his heart: 'Hari never stops his teasing.' Hearing these very dear words of his dear friend, he sent Bhringi to call all his followers.

first: सिव अनुसासन सुनि सब आये। प्रभु-पद-जलज सीस तिन्ह नाये॥
en: Hearing Shiva's order they all came and bowed their heads at the Lord's lotus feet. Seeing his own company, with their many mounts and many strange forms, Shiva laughed.

first: कोउ मुख-हीन बिपुल-मुख काहू। बिनु-पद-कर कोउ बहु-पद-बाहू॥
en: Some had no mouth and some had many mouths. Some had no hands or feet, others had many feet and arms. Some had many eyes and some had none. Some were very fat and some very thin.

first: तन-खीन कोउ अति-पीन पावन, कोउ अपावन गति धरे।
en: Some were thin and some very stout, some clean and some unclean in their ways. They wore frightful ornaments, held skulls in their hands, and were smeared with fresh blood. They had the faces of donkeys, dogs, pigs and jackals; who can count their endless forms? The many kinds of ghosts, goblins and yoginis cannot be described.

first: सो॰—नाचहिँ गावहिँ गीत, परम तरङ्गी भूत सब।
en: All the ghosts danced and sang songs in high spirits. They looked very odd and spoke in strange ways.

first: चौ॰—जस दूलह तस बनी बराता। कौतुक बिबिध हाेहिँ भग जाता॥
en: The wedding party was just like the groom, and many funny things happened along the way. Here, Himachal had built a wedding hall so wonderful that it cannot be described.

first: सैल सकल जहँ लगि जग माहीँ। लघु बिसाल नहिँ वरनि सिराहीँ॥
en: All the mountains in the world, small and great, more than can be counted, and all the forests, seas, rivers and lakes, were invited by Himachal.

first: कामरूप सुन्दर तनु धारी। सहित समाज साेह बर नारी॥
en: Taking lovely forms as they wished, they came with their beautiful wives and families to Himachal's home, and all sang auspicious songs with love.

first: प्रयमहिँ गिरि बहु गृह सँवराये। जथाजोग जहँ तहँ सब छाये॥
en: The mountain king had already had many houses decorated, and all the guests were lodged in fitting places. Seeing the beauty of the city, even the Creator's skill seemed small.

first: लघु लागि बिधि की निपुनता, अवलोकि पुर सोभा सही।
en: Seeing the true beauty of the city, Brahma's skill seemed small. Forests, gardens, wells, lakes and rivers were all lovely; who could describe them? Every house shone with many auspicious arches, flags and banners. The handsome, clever, graceful men and women charmed even the minds of sages.

first: दो॰—जगदम्बा जहँ अवतरी, सो पुर बरनि कि जाइ।
en: Can the city where the Mother of the world was born be described? Wealth, powers, riches and every joy kept growing there day by day.

first: चौ॰—नगर निकट बरात जब आई। पुर खरभर सोभा अधिकाई॥
en: When the wedding party came near the city, there was a happy bustle and the city looked even finer. People decorated themselves and their many mounts and went out with respect to welcome the guests.

first: हिय हरषे सुर-सेन निहारी। हरिहि देखि अति भये सुखारी॥
en: They were glad at heart to see the army of gods, and very happy to see Vishnu. But when they began to see Shiva's company, all their animals took fright and ran away.

first: धरि धीरज तहाँ रहे सयाने। बालक सब लेइ जीव पराने॥
en: The grown-ups kept their courage and stayed, but all the children ran for their lives. When they reached home and their parents asked them, they spoke trembling with fear.

first: कहिय काह कहि जाइ न बाता। जम कर धारि किधौँ बरियाता॥
en: 'What can we say? It cannot be put into words. Is this the army of Yama, or a wedding party? The groom is mad and rides a bull. Snakes, skulls and ashes are his ornaments.'

first: तन छार ब्याल कपाल भूषन, नगन जटिल भयङ्करा।
en: 'Ash on his body, snakes and skulls for ornaments, naked, with matted hair, and frightening! With him are ghosts, goblins, yoginis and fierce-faced demons. Whoever stays alive after seeing this party has truly great merit, and only he will see Uma's wedding.' This is what the children said in every house.

first: दो॰—समुझि महेस समाज सब, जननि जनक मुसुकाहिँ।
en: Understanding that this was Shiva's company, the mothers and fathers smiled. They comforted the children in many ways: 'Do not be afraid; there is nothing to fear.'

first: चौ॰—लेइ अगवान बरातहि आये। दिये सबहि जनवास सुहाये॥
en: The welcoming party brought the guests in and gave them all pleasant lodgings. Maina prepared a lovely lamp offering, and the women with her sang auspicious songs.

first: कञ्चनथार साेह बर पानी। परिछन चली हरहि हरषानी॥
en: Holding a golden plate in her fair hand, she went happily to welcome Hara with the lamp. But when the women saw Rudra's frightful form, great fear arose in their hearts.

first: भागि भवन पैठी अति त्रासा। गये महेस जहाँ जनवासा॥
en: They ran into the house in great terror, and Shiva went on to the guests' lodging. Maina felt deep sorrow in her heart, and she called for the mountain king's daughter.

first: अधिक सनेह गोद बैठारी। स्याम-सरोज नयन भरि बारी ॥
en: With great love she sat her on her lap, her dark lotus eyes full of tears: 'The Creator who gave you such beauty, how could that fool make your groom a madman?'

first: कस कीन्ह बर बौराह बिधि जेहि, तुम्हहिँ सुन्दरता दई।
en: 'How could the Creator who gave you such beauty make your groom a madman? The fruit meant for the wishing tree is being forced to grow on a thorny babul bush. I would rather leap from a mountain with you, burn in fire or drown in the sea. Let our home be ruined and our name disgraced in the world, but while I live I will not allow this marriage.'

first: दो॰—भई बिकल अबला सकल, दुखित देखि गिरि-नारि।
en: Seeing the mountain queen in grief, all the women became distressed. Thinking of their love for the girl, they wept, wailed and cried out.

first: चौ॰—नारद कर मैं काह बिगारा। भवन मोर जिन्ह बसत उजारा॥
en: 'What harm did I ever do to Narada, that he has ruined my happy home? He gave Uma such advice that she did penance for a mad groom.'

first: साँचेहु उनके मोह न माया। उदासीन धन धाम न जाया॥
en: 'Truly he has no attachment or love, no wealth, house or wife; he cares for nothing. He feels no shame or fear in ruining other people's homes. How can a barren woman know the pain of childbirth?'

first: जननिहिँ विकल बिलोकि भवानी। बोली जुत-बिबेक मृदु बानी॥
en: Seeing her mother so upset, Bhavani spoke gentle, wise words: 'Mother, think this over and do not grieve. What the Creator has planned cannot be changed.'

first: करम लिखा जौँ बाउर नाहू। तौ कत दोष लगाइय काहू॥
en: 'If a mad husband is written in my fate, why should anyone be blamed? Can you wipe out what the Creator has written? Mother, do not take blame on yourself for nothing.'

first: जनि लेहु मातु कलङ्क करुना,-परिहरहु अवसर नहीँ।
en: 'Mother, do not take this blame on yourself; stop grieving, this is not the time for it. Whatever joy or sorrow is written on my forehead, I will find it wherever I go.' Hearing Uma's humble, gentle words, all the women were troubled; they blamed the Creator in many ways and shed tears.

first: दो॰—तेहि अवसर नारद सहित, अरु रिषि-सप्त समेत।
en: At that moment, hearing the news, Himavan came quickly into the house with Narada and the seven sages.

first: चौ॰—तब नारद सबही समुझावा। पूरब-कथा-प्रसङ्ग सुनावा॥
en: Then Narada calmed everyone and told them the story of her past life: 'Maina, hear my true words. Your daughter Bhavani is the Mother of the world.'

first: अजा अनादि-सक्ति अबिनासिनि। सदा सम्भु अरघङ्ग-निवासिनि॥
en: 'She is unborn, the eternal first Power, never destroyed, always dwelling as half of Shiva's body. She creates, keeps and ends the world, and takes a body by her own will for play.'

first: जनमी प्रथम दच्छ-गृह जाई। नाम सती सुन्दर तनु पाई॥
en: 'First she was born in Daksha's house, named Sati, with a lovely form. There too Sati was married to Shankar; the story is known all over the world.'

first: एक बार आवत सिव सङ्गा। देखेड़ रघुकुल कमल पतङ्गा॥
en: 'Once, while coming back with Shiva, she saw Rama, the sun to the lotus of the Raghu family. She fell into delusion, did not obey Shiva, and in her confusion took the form of Sita.'

first: सिय बेष सती जो कीन्ह तेहि, अपराध सङ्कर परिहरी।
en: 'Because Sati took Sita's form, Shankar gave her up for that fault. Then, in grief at being parted from Hara, she went to her father's sacrifice and burnt herself in the fire of yoga. Now, born in your house, she has done hard penance to win her own husband. Knowing this, give up your doubt: Girija is forever Shankar's beloved.'

first: दो॰—सुनि नारद के बचन तब, सब कर मिटा विषाद।
en: Hearing Narada's words, everyone's sorrow vanished. In a moment the news spread through the whole city, from house to house.

first: चौ॰—तब मैना हिमवन्त अनन्दे। पुनि पुनि पारवती-पद बन्दे।
en: Then Maina and Himavan rejoiced and bowed again and again at Parvati's feet. Men and women, children, young people and elders, all the people of the city were overjoyed.

first: लगे होन पुर मङ्गल गाना। सजे सबहिँ हाटक-घट नाना॥
en: Auspicious songs began in the city, and everyone set out golden pots of many kinds. Feasts of many kinds were prepared, following the rules of the art of cooking.

first: सो जेवनार कि जाइ बखानी। बसहिँ भवन जेहि मातु भवानी॥
en: Can that feast be described, made in the house where Mother Bhavani lived? With respect they invited the whole wedding party, Vishnu, Brahma and gods of every kind.

first: बिबिध पाँति बैठी जेवनारा। लगे परोसन निपुन सुआरा॥
en: Many rows sat down to the feast, and skilled cooks began to serve. Knowing the gods were eating, the women began to sing teasing wedding songs in sweet voices.

first: गारी मधुर सुर देहिँ सुन्दरि, व्यङ्ग बचन सुनावहीँ।
en: The lovely women sang sweet teasing songs full of playful jokes. The gods ate very slowly, enjoying the fun. The joy that grew during the meal could not be told even with millions of mouths. After they had washed, they were given betel leaves and each went to his own lodging.

first: दो॰—बहुरि मुनिन्ह हिमवन्त कहँ, लगन सुनाई आइ।
en: Then the sages came and told Himavan the wedding hour. Seeing that the time for the wedding had come, he sent for the gods.

first: चौ॰—बोलि सकल सुर सादर लीन्हे। सबहि जयोचित आसन दीन्हे॥
en: He respectfully called all the gods and gave each a fitting seat. The altar was prepared by Vedic rule, and the lovely women sang auspicious songs.

first: सिंहासन अति दिब्य सुहावा। जाइ न बरनि बिचित्र बनावा॥
en: Shiva bowed to the Brahmins, remembered his own Lord Rama in his heart, and sat on a most heavenly, lovely throne whose wonderful make cannot be described.

first: बहुरि मुनीसन्ह उमा बोलाई। करि सिङ्गार सखी लेइ आई॥
en: Then the great sages called Uma, and her friends brought her, adorned. Seeing her beauty all the gods were charmed. What poet in the world could describe such loveliness?

first: जगदम्बिका जानि भव-भामा। सुरन्ह मनहिं मन कीन्ह प्रनामा॥
en: Knowing her to be the Mother of the world and Shiva's wife, the gods bowed to her in their hearts. Bhavani is the very limit of beauty; even millions of mouths cannot describe her.

first: कोटिहु बदन नहिँ बनइ बरनत, जग-जननि-साेभा महा।
en: The great beauty of the Mother of the world cannot be told even with millions of mouths. The Vedas, Shesha and Sarasvati shrink from describing it; what then can dull-witted Tulsi say?

first: छबि-खानि मातु भवानि गवनी, मध्य मंडप सिव जहाँ।
en: Mother Bhavani, a mine of beauty, went to the middle of the wedding hall where Shiva was. Out of shyness she could not look at her husband's lotus feet, but her mind, like a bee, stayed there.

first: दो॰—मुनि अनुसासन गनपतिहि, पूजेउ सम्मु-भवानि।
en: At the sages' bidding, Shiva and Bhavani worshipped Ganesha. Let no one who hears this have doubts; know in your heart that the gods are without beginning.

first: चौ॰—जसि बिबाह के बिधि खुति गाई। महामुनिन्ह सो सब करवाई॥
en: The great sages had every wedding rite done just as the Vedas teach. The mountain king took kusha grass and his daughter's hand, and gave her to Bhava, knowing her to be Bhavani.

first: पानि-ग्रहन जब कीन्ह महेसा। हिय हरषे तब सकल सुरेसा॥
en: When Mahesha took her hand, all the lords of the gods rejoiced in their hearts. The great sages chanted Vedic hymns, and the gods cried, 'Victory, victory, victory to Shankar!'

first: बाजहिँ बाजन विबिध बिधाना। सुमन बृष्टि नभ भइ बिधि नाना॥
en: Music of many kinds played, and flowers of many kinds rained from the sky. So Hara and Girija were married, and joy filled all the worlds.

first: दासी दास तुरग रथ नागा। धेनु बसन मनि बस्तु विभागा॥
en: Maids and servants, horses, chariots, elephants, cows, clothes, jewels and many goods, and carts full of grain and golden vessels: the dowry he gave cannot be described.

first: दाइज दियाे बहु भाँति पुनि कर,-जोरि हिम-भूधर कह्यो।
en: After giving a rich dowry of many kinds, the snowy mountain joined his hands and said, 'Shankar, you lack nothing; what can I give you?' and he held on to his lotus feet. Shiva, the ocean of mercy, comforted his father-in-law in every way. Then Maina, her heart full of love, held his lotus feet.

first: दो॰—नाथ उमा मम प्रान प्रिय, गृह-किङ्करी करेहु।
en: 'Lord, Uma is dear to me as my life; keep her as a servant in your house. Forgive all our faults, and now be pleased and grant me this boon.'

first: चौ॰—बहु बिधि सम्भु सास समुझाई। गवनी भवन चरन सिर नाई॥
en: Shiva comforted his mother-in-law in many ways, and she bowed at his feet and went inside. Then the mother called Uma, took her on her lap and gave her good advice.

first: करेहु सदा सङ्कर-पद-पूजा। नारि धरम पति-देव न दूजा॥
en: 'Always worship Shankar's feet. For a wife, there is no duty other than to treat her husband as her god.' As she spoke, her eyes filled with tears, and she held her daughter to her heart again.

first: कत बिधि सृजी नारि जग माहीँ। पराधीन सपनेहुँ सुख माहीं॥
en: 'Why did the Creator make women in this world? Living under others' control, they never know happiness, not even in dreams.' The mother was overcome with love, but, thinking it was not the time for grief, she kept her courage.

first: पुनि पुनि मिलति परति गहि चरना। परम प्रेम कछु जाइ न वरना॥
en: Again and again she hugged her and fell at her feet; her deep love cannot be described. Bhavani met and embraced all the women, then went and clung to her mother's breast again.

first: जननिहि बहुरि मिलि चली उचित असीस सब काहू दई।
en: After meeting her mother once more she set off, and everyone gave her fitting blessings. She kept turning back to look at her mother; then her friends took her to Shiva. Shankar satisfied all who begged gifts and set out for home with Uma. All the gods rejoiced and rained flowers, and fine drums sounded in the sky.

first: दो॰—चले सङ्ग हिमवन्त तब, पहुँचावन अति हेतु।
en: Then Himavan, with great love, went along to see them off. The bull-bannered Shiva comforted him in many ways and sent him back.

first: चौ॰—तुरत भवन आये गिरिराई। सकल सैल सर लिये बोलाई॥
en: The mountain king came home at once and called all the mountains and lakes. Himavan honoured them with respect, gifts and kind words, and sent them all off.

first: जबहिं सम्भु कैलासहि आये। सुर सब निज निज लोक सिधाये॥
en: When Shiva reached Kailasa, all the gods went back to their own worlds. Shiva and Bhavani are the mother and father of the world, so I do not describe their love play.

first: करहिँ बिबिध बिधि भोग बिलासा। गनन्ह समेत बसहिँ कैलासा॥
en: They enjoyed many pleasures and lived on Kailasa with their attendants. The joys of Hara and Girija were new every day, and in this way a long time passed.

first: तब जनमेउ षट-बदन-कुमारा। तारक असुर समर जेहि मारा॥
en: Then the six-faced son was born, who killed the demon Taraka in battle. The birth of the six-faced one is famous in the Vedas, scriptures and Puranas, and the whole world knows it.

first: जग जान षनमुख जनम करम प्रताप पुरुषारथ महा।
en: The world knows the birth, deeds, glory and great courage of the six-faced one, so I have told the story of Shiva's son only briefly. Men and women who tell or sing of this marriage of Uma and Shambhu will always find joy and blessing in weddings and all good works.

first: दो॰—चरित-सिन्धु गिरिजारवन, बेद न पावहिँ पार।
en: The deeds of Girija's beloved are an ocean whose far shore even the Vedas cannot reach. How then can Tulsidas, a dull-witted simple man, describe them?

first: चौ॰—सम्भु चरित सुनि सरस सुहावा। भरद्वाज मुनि अति सुख पावा॥
en: Hearing this sweet and lovely story of Shambhu, the sage Bharadvaja felt great joy. His longing for the story grew strong; tears filled his eyes and the hair on his body stood on end.

first: प्रेम बिबस मुख आव न बानी। दसा देखि हरषे मुनि-ज्ञानी॥
en: Overcome by love, he could not speak. Seeing his state, the wise sage Yajnavalkya was glad: 'Oh great sage, blessed is your birth, for the lord of Gauri is dear to you as your life.'

first: सिव-पद-कमल जिन्हहिँ रति नाहीं। रामहिँ ते सपनेहुँ न सुहाहीँ॥
en: 'Those who have no love for Shiva's lotus feet never please Rama, not even in dreams. Sincere love for the feet of Vishvanatha, lord of the world, is the mark of a devotee of Rama.'

first: सिव सम को रघुपति-ब्रत-धारी। बिनु अघ तजी सत्ती असि नारी॥
en: 'Who keeps the vow of devotion to Rama like Shiva, who gave up such a wife as Sati though she had done no other wrong? He took a vow and made devotion to Rama firm. Brother, who is as dear to Rama as Shiva?'

first: दो॰—प्रथमहिँ कहि मैँ सिव चरित, बूझा मरम तुम्हार।
en: 'That is why I told Shiva's story first, to learn your secret heart. You are a pure servant of Rama, free from every fault.'

first: चौ॰—मैँ जाना तुम्हार गुन सीला। कहउँ सुनहु अब रघुपति-लीला॥
en: 'I have come to know your virtue and good nature. Now listen, I will tell the deeds of Rama. Hear, sage: the joy in my mind at meeting you today cannot be told.'

first: रामचरित अति अमित मुनीसा। कहि न सकहिँ सतकोटि अहीसा॥
en: 'Great sage, Rama's story is endless; even millions of Sheshas could not tell it. Still, remembering the Lord of speech, Rama with the bow in hand, I will tell it as I have heard it.'

first: सारद दारु-नारि-सम स्वामी। राम-सूत्रधर अन्तरजामी॥
en: 'Sarasvati is like a wooden puppet, and Rama, the Lord who lives in all hearts, holds the strings. When he sees someone as his own and shows grace, he makes speech dance in the courtyard of that poet's heart.'

first: प्रनवउँ सोइ कृपाल रघुनाथा। बरनउँ विषद तासु गुन गाथा॥
en: 'I bow to that kind Lord of the Raghus and tell the pure story of his virtues. Kailasa, best of mountains, is most lovely, where Shiva and Uma always live.'

first: दो॰—सिद्ध तपोधन जोगि जन, सुर किन्नर मुनि बृन्द।
en: 'Siddhas, ascetics, yogis, gods, kinnaras and crowds of sages, all virtuous souls, live there and serve Shiva, the root of joy.'

first: चौ॰—हरि-हर-विमुख धरम रति नाहीँ। ते नर तहँ सपनेहुँ नहिँ जाहोँ।
en: 'Those who turn away from Hari and Hara and do not love dharma never go there, even in dreams. On that mountain stands a huge banyan tree, ever fresh and lovely in every season.'

first: त्रिविध समीर सुसीतल छाया। सिव-बिस्राम बिटप स्रुति गाया॥
en: 'Cool, gentle, fragrant breezes blow there, and its shade is pleasant; the Vedas call it Shiva's resting tree. Once the Lord went under it, and on seeing the tree his heart was filled with joy.'

first: निज कर डासि नाग-रिपु-छाला। बैठे सहजहिँ सम्भु कृपाला॥
en: 'With his own hands the kind Shambhu spread a tiger skin and sat down at ease. His body was fair as the jasmine, the moon and the conch; his arms were long, and he wore a sage's bark cloth.'

first: तरुन-अरुन-अम्बुज सम चरना। नख-दुति भगत-हृदय-तम-हरना।
en: 'His feet were like fresh red lotuses, and the glow of his toenails removes the darkness from devotees' hearts. The enemy of Tripura wore snakes and ash as ornaments, and his face outshone the autumn moon.'

first: दो॰—जटा-मुकुट-सुरसरित सिर, लोचन नलिन बिसाल।
en: 'On his head was a crown of matted hair with the heavenly river Ganga; his eyes were large like lotuses. Blue-throated and full of beauty, he had a young crescent moon shining on his brow.'

first: चौ॰—बैठे साेह काम-रिपुं कैसे। घरे सरीर सान्त-रस जैसे।
en: 'The enemy of Kama, seated there, looked like the spirit of peace in bodily form. Seeing it was a good moment, Mother Bhavani, Parvati, went to Shambhu.'

first: जानि प्रिया आदर अति कीन्हा। बाम-भाग आसन हर दीन्हा।
en: 'Knowing her as his beloved, Hara greeted her with great respect and gave her a seat at his left side. She sat happily near Shiva, and the story of her former life came to her mind.'

first: पति-हिय-हेतु अधिक मन मानी। बिहँसि उमा बोली मृदु बानी॥
en: 'Feeling in her heart that her husband loved her more than ever, Uma smiled and spoke softly. The mountain's daughter wished to ask about the story that does good to all the worlds.'

first: बिस्वनाथ मम-नाथ पुरारी। त्रिभुवन महिमा बिदित तुम्हारी॥
en: 'Lord of the world, my Lord, enemy of Tripura, your glory is known in all three worlds. Moving and unmoving beings, serpents, men and gods all serve your lotus feet.'

first: दो॰—प्रभु समरथ सरबज्ञ सिव, सकल कला-गुन धाम।
en: 'Lord Shiva, you are all-powerful and all-knowing, the home of every art and virtue, a treasure of yoga, knowledge and detachment. Your name is a wishing tree for those who bow to you.'
